 : JUDGMENT :
The respondent/SLAO, Karnataka Housing Board, Bengaluru, has made this reference under Section 77(1) L.A.C. No. 43/2020 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'RFCTLA Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.32/7 measuring 1.01 acres of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of construction of houses.
Preliminary notification was issued on 19.03.2011.
Final notification was published in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
The award was passed on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.1,09,87,312/-.

As the suit in O.S.No.585/2013 in respect of the said property is pending for adjudication before Prl. Senior Judge and CJM, Ramanagara, the L.A.O. has sent the reference to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.1,09,87,312/-.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Karnataka Grameena Bank, Hosakote Branch, Bengaluru Rural District.
After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to the claimant and Objectors.
All the claimant and objectors have entered appearance through their counsels.
The claimant has filed claim statement.

.4. Claimant - M.V. Doddaveeraiah @ Veeresh has filed claim statement stating that the respondent acquired the property bearing Sy. No. 32/7 measuring 1 acre 01 guntas of Byalalu village and passed the award in case No. KHB/LAQ/5 (32/7)/2010-11 dated 25.02.2020.

Further stated that as there was objectors, who have filed objections for payment of the award amount to the claimant, the respondent referred the matter to this Court and deposited the award amount of Rs.1,09,87,312/-.
Further the said property was owned and possessed by claimant at the time of acquisition of land.

Further the said acquired property has been purchased by claimant under the registered sale deed dated 06.03.2008 for valuable consideration from one Munihanumaiah and thereafter khatha has been changed in his name.

Further stated that originally the L.A.C. No. 43/2020 land in Sy. No.
32/7 was belonged to one Veerachannaiah @ Earachannaiah and after his death, the land in question mutated in the name of his son M.V. Channakeshava, in turn, he sold the said land to Smt.
M.K. Thimmakka through registered sale deed dated 06.03.2008 and thereafter the said M.K.
Thimmakka sold the said property in favour of claimant.

Further stated that one Chikkamuniyaiah and others had filed a suit in O.S. No.585/2013 against Munihanumaiah and others including claimant before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Ramanagara for partition and separate possession in respect of the above referred acquired property.

Hence, prays to release the award amount.

The Objectors 1, 2, 3(a) to (d) and 4 to 6 filed claim statement stating that they admitted and confirmed the claim statement filed by claimant and they have no objections to disburse the award amount with accrued interest to the claimant.
Further stated that they have no claim in respect of the acquired land in Sy. No.32/7 measuring 1 acre 3 guntas of land of Byalalu village.
Hence, they prayed to release the compensation amount in favour of claimant.
.6. The Objectors 7 to 12 and 13 (a) to (c) filed separate memo stating that they have no objection to disburse the award amount with interest in favour of claimant.
.7. In order to prove their case, the claimant is examined as PW.1.

The documents got marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
.8.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimant proves that he is the absolute owner of the L.A.C. No.
43/2020 acquired property and entitled for the compensation?"
.9.

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS .10.

This is a reference made by the respondent to the Court under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: The property involved in this case is the property bearing Sy. No. 32/7 measuring 1 acre 1 gunta of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka and the said property has been acquired in case No.KHB/LAQ/5(32/7)/2010-11 dated 25.02.2020.
This reference is made in view of the pendency of case in respect of the property in Sy. No.32/7 and other properties.

Subsequent to the reference of this case to the Court, the Court issued notice to all the claimant L.A.C. No. 43/2020 and Objectors who were objected the compensation in favour of khathedars before the LAO.
.11.
The Objectors 1 to 12 and 13(a) to (c) filed separate statements and memos on various dates stating that they have no objection to give compensation to the claimant.
Only the claimant filed claim statement as well as led evidence in support of his claim statement and examined as PW.1 and also got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Ex.P.1 is the sale deed dated 06.03.2008 executed in favour of claimant by one Smt. M.K. Thimmakka with her minor son.

As per the said sale deed,
the property bearing Sy. No.32/7 measuring 1 acre 1 gunta of land of Byalalu village has been sold in favour of claimant.

On the basis of the said sale deed, the property has been mutated in the name of claimant and also the document shows that claimant is the khathedar of the acquired property as on the date of acquisition and even prior to acquisition from the date of aforesaid sale deed.

Ex.P.7 is the order Doddaveeraiah M V Alias Veeresh vs Slao, Karnataka Housing Board, ... on 7 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38040150/
5 sheet in O.S.No.702/2014 on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge L.A.C. No. 43/2020 and CJM, Ramanagara.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of pendency of the said suit, the LAO has referred the case to the Court and the award amount has been deposited to the Court.
As per the said order sheet Ex.P.7, the plaintiffs therein filed a memo on 27.09.2021 stating that they are not pressing the suit and hence the said suit in O.S.No.702/2014 has been dismissed.
In the said suit, the claimant is the defendant No.7.
As the said suit in O.S.No.702/2014 has been disposed off, now there is no other dispute pending between claimants.

.12. Apart from that, on 28.09.2022 the Objector No.12(a) to (c) filed statement stating that they are not claiming any compensation in respect of acquired property and they have no objections to pay the compensation in favour of claimant.

Similarly,
on 28.09.2022 the objectors 10 and 11 filed a memo stating that they are not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

Similarly, on 19.11.2022 the Objector No.9 filed a memo stating that he has no objection to pay the L.A.C. No. 43/2020 compensation to the claimant and he is not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

Similarly, on 28.02.2023 the Objector No.7 filed a memo stating that he has no objection to pay the compensation to the claimant and he is not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

As such, except claimant,
the Objectors are not claiming any right over the acquired property.
In the case on hand, acquisition of property in Sy. No.32/7 measuring 1 acre 1 gunta of Byalalu village is not in dispute and also depositing of compensation amount is not in dispute.
Except claimant, nobody is claiming right over the said property and compensation amount.
The suit pending before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge at Ramanagara Court disposed off, when the acquisition proceedings has been commenced.

Therefore,
this Court is of the humble opinion that the claimant is an absolute owner of the acquired property and the documents also standing in the name of claimant even according to the materials placed by the respondent as L.A.C. No. 43/2020 well as claimant.
As such, the claimant is entitled for compensation in view of the acquired property involved in this case as claimant is the absolute owner of the acquired property.
Hence, I answer above point in the affirmative.

In the result I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 in respect of claimant is hereby allowed.
